newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM nominee keeps quiet on king's stand.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM nominee keeps quiet on king's stand.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Hout said on Tuesday he would not comment on King Norodom Sihanouk's refusal to recognise his nomination as first prime minister.
Sihanouk said on Monday he would not recognise Ung Huot as first prime minister because the position belonged to his son, Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"I have no reaction at this stage," Ung Huot told reporters. "I must be silent."
Ung Huot, a senior member of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party, said he had yet to see the king's comments, which were released in Beijing late on Monday.
Sihanouk said Ranariddh had the right to retain the title of first prime minister unless he was formally condemned by an independent Cambodian tribunal.
"While maintaining my affection for him, I will abstain from giving His Excellency Mr Ung Huot his new title of 'first prime minister'," Sihanouk said in comments released to news agencies.

Ranariddh has also opposed the foreign minister's candidacy, and announced at the weekend that Ung Huot was being temporarily expelled from his royalist FUNCINPEC party. But Ung Huot dismissed the move as a desperate joke.
Ranariddh left Cambodia on the eve of his overthrow by powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on July 5-6.

Hun Sen, who backs Ung Huot's nomination as first prime minister, said the prince was free to return to Cambodia, but he would have to face trial for alleged illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and for alleged weapons smuggling.

Many FUNCINPEC members and supporters fled the country in the wake of Ranariddh's ouster and the subsequent crackdown on his supporters in which some 40 people were killed, according to human rights investigators.
Ung Huot was nominated to replace Ranariddh by FUNCINPEC members who remained in Cambodia.
About 20 members of FUNCINPEC and a small allied party were absent when the 120-member National Assembly was convened on Monday.
Sihanouk said Ung Huot's appointment by an incomplete parliament would be invalid.

"The decisions of an incomplete parliament working under conditions of very questionable 'freedom' and 'regularity' could not be considered valid within the spirit of our 1993 Constitution and our liberal democracy," he said.
Meanwhile, National Assembly President Chea Sim on Monday called for Ung Huot to be approved as first prime minister in place of Ranariddh.
Cambodian assembly officials said administrative delays meant voting on Ung Huot's nomination might be delayed until next week.

Ranariddh arrived in Beijing on Friday for what officials insist is a private visit with his father, who is receiving medical treatment there. The king maintains a palatial residence in the Chinese capital.
In his faxed comments, Sihanouk said he was still too ill to return to his troubled Southeast Asian homeland.
But the king made clear he was taking a keen interest in the affairs of the nation, over which he reigns but does not rule.
In an apparent recognition of Hun Sen's political grip on Cambodia, Sihanouk stressed he would not oppose laws passed since the second prime minister seized control.
As a constitutional monarch, he was obliged to let parliament chief and acting head of state Chea Sim choose which laws to sign into effect, Sihanouk said.
